card: Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC method for encrypting existing unencrypted wallets, requiring -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet ahead of planned removal. Post-creation encryption carries footguns: unencrypted key material may linger on disk, new keys generated after encryption invalidate earlier backups, and encrypting wallets with imported descriptors can alter spending conditions unexpectedly (#26607). Creating encrypted wallets from inception using createwallet remains fully supported. Functional tests are refactored to set up encrypted wallets at creation time rather than encrypting existing ones.
evidence: RFC issue #36027: '[rfc] Remove encrypting wallets that already exist'
PR description citing #26607: 'Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user.'
problem: Encrypting a wallet after creation has severe footguns: unencrypted key material often remains on persistent storage, regenerating keys upon encryption invalidates earlier backups (risking fund loss), and encrypting wallets containing manually imported descriptors can change spending conditions unexpectedly (#26607).

risk.why: Deprecating an existing RPC breaks external scripts or user workflows that encrypt wallets after creation unless the deprecation flag is supplied.

scope_notes: The C++ change in `src/wallet/rpc/encrypt.cpp` is only 5 lines; the majority of the diff consists of test framework helper updates and test refactorings to avoid post-creation encryption.
summary: Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC method, requiring nodes to be started with `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` to use it. Refactors the functional test suite to create encrypted wallets upfront via `createwallet` with a passphrase instead of encrypting existing wallets, while gating tests of `encryptwallet` behind the deprecation flag.
